thread:
maya (PM): Hey team — customer asks piling up around streaming behavior. Can we align on an MVP for chat streaming (SSE vs WS), delta payload shape, and finish reasons? We need launch criteria for Hosted API and a clear rollback/fallback plan.

alex (eng): Short version: WebSockets give bidirectional control (ping/pong, finer flow control), SSE is simpler for short-lived browser clients and works with existing HTTP infra. Both can work, but semantics matter: how we represent deltas and finish reasons.

rene (eng-ml): For model runtime, we already emit token deltas and a final finish signal. Question is API surface: do we stream full messages (role + content updates), or only 'delta' fragments? Also how to surface tool/function calls mid-stream.

maya (PM): Proposed MVP scope: 1) SSE for Hosted API (simple to integrate for most customers), 2) WS as opt-in for Dedicated/Private later, 3) delta format: small structured events with type ("delta", "tool_call", "finish"). Acceptance: docs + SDK sample, 2 customer pilots, error behavior documented. Thoughts?

alex (eng): +1 on starting with SSE for Hosted. Implementation note: SSE uses `event:` and `data:` lines which map nicely to single JSON payloads per event. Example: 
```
event: delta
data: {"id":"abc","type":"delta","role":"assistant","delta":"Hello"}

```
Pro: easy to proxy and debug. Con: harder to do client-initiated cancels (but can use `POST /responses/{id}/cancel`).

rene (eng-ml): On delta content: prefer a canonical shape so SDKs can reassemble reliably. Suggest: { "type": "delta", "delta": [{"role":"assistant"},{"content":"text","fragment":"Hello"}], "cursor": 123 } — but we should avoid nested arrays/objects in the public stream payload. Keep it flat-ish: { "type":"delta","role":"assistant","content":"Hello" }.

tara (design): From UX: we need clear client hook for partial render vs incremental function-call args. For function calling during stream: emit `tool_call` events with `name` and `args_fragment`. Clients must be able to present partial tool args (e.g., streaming file content).

liam (support): Important customer asks: 1) enterprise customers want a definitive finish reason enum for auditing (must map to model-level finish reasons plus our own: `stop`, `error`, `length`, `fallback`). 2) They expect stable streaming JSON shape so our parsers don't break on minor changes.

maya (PM): Draft finish_reason enum: `stop` (model signaled completion), `length` (truncated by token/length limit), `error` (runtime/model error), `fallback` (we switched to a fallback model due to capacity), `cancel` (user or client cancel). These strings must appear in final `finish` event.

alex (eng): Agree. Implementation detail for SSE final event: `event: finish
data: {"type":"finish","reason":"stop","message_id":"abc","meta":{}}` — meta must be optional and stable. Also recommend sequence numbers on deltas: `seq` so clients can detect missing pieces.

rene (eng-ml): On ordering: seq numbers are good. Also include `partial_token_count` maybe not needed. For model-initiated tool calls, we should allow interleaving: deltas -> tool_call fragments -> deltas -> finish. Document clearly.

maya (PM): Launch criteria checklist (Hosted API MVP):
- API spec shipped (SSE) + examples for JS/browser + curl
- SDKs (python/js) implement streaming reassembly helpers
- 2 pilot customers onboarded and validated output consistency
- Error and fallback behavior documented (how clients see `fallback` finish_reason)
- Canary rollout with telemetry to monitor latency and reassembly errors

alex (eng): Rollback/fallback plan: if streaming causes regressions, we can: 1) revert streaming flag for affected model routes, 2) provide non-streaming full response endpoints (existing). Also expose a header `x-rw-streaming-enabled: true/false` in logs.

tara (design): SDK UX: provide high-level `onDelta`, `onToolCall`, `onFinish` callbacks and a `reassemble()` helper. Examples in README.

liam (support): Also add a troubleshooting doc for `missing seq` and `partial args` edge cases — customers will hit this first.

deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: canary to 10% on Hosted region `us-west-2` at 2026-06-15T03:00Z.

maya (PM): Open questions to decide now: A) Should we include `content_type` per delta (e.g., text/html vs text/plain vs json) or keep plain text and add structured output events? B) Do we standardize on SSE-only payloads for MVP or publish WS contract now too?

alex (eng): A) add optional `content_type` in delta but default to `text`. Keep it optional. B) publish WS contract as draft but ship SSE-only MVP. We can reuse same JSON event shape for WS frames later.

rene (eng-ml): One more: cost/throughput implications of seq and meta sizes — keep events compact. Avoid verbose `meta` by default.

maya (PM): OK — decision summary (MVP):
- SSE-only for Hosted API; WS drafted later
- Compact event JSON with fields: `type`, `seq`, `role?`, `content?`, `tool_call?`, `finish_reason?`, `message_id`
- Finish reasons: `stop`, `length`, `error`, `fallback`, `cancel`
- SDK helpers + docs + 2 pilots + canary rollout

Can everyone react with :thumbsup: if they agree or flag specific objections. We'll lock spec tomorrow and open PR to docs.

alex (eng): :thumbsup:

rene (eng-ml): :thumbsup:

liam (support): :thumbsup: add troubleshooting doc to the plan

tara (design): :thumbsup: will draft SDK example screens

maya (PM): Thanks — I'll create spec PR and link customers for pilots.
